notes: Works and passes, but the squashfs single-file-root detection with expectedRemote is convoluted and the zip Open gets an unnecessary symlink-only special case for offsets past EOF.

Production code is identical to the reference and docs are added; tests are adequate but thin for zip (no range or .rclonelink-regular coverage), and the squashfs test depends on an external mksquashfs binary.

The zip change matches the reference; squashfs gets a clean Readlink-based approach with newObjectNative refactored so links match only by suffixed name, and it adds docs and good unit tests plus a hostile-archive end-to-end test.

Core listing, reading and NewObject behaviour are right, but a root pointing at a .rclonelink name is not detected as a single file, a missing link target is silently treated as empty, and changing f.file to o.Remote() risks regressing file roots in subdirectories.
Byte-for-byte the same as C3: reference-equivalent code plus docs and modest tests, with the squashfs test relying on mksquashfs.

Silently drops zip members under or shadowing symlink names when --links is on, so the listing changes for non-symlink entries and a hidden test fails; it also adds complex root/rootIsLink handling and an ad-hoc Open special case.

Correct and robust for both backends, and it also handles symlink/regular name clashes so listing and NewObject agree, but it reads every zip link target eagerly when the archive is opened (extra I/O on remote archives) and adds shared archiver helpers the task did not need.
